subject: Clarify billing granularity, context-siloing, and minimums
messages:
From: Tom Harris <tom.harris@brightcart.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on billing granularity and minimums

Hi Jordan,

Quick follow-up from the procurement review: our finance team flagged a few items in the draft SOW around billing units. Before we move to signatures, can you confirm these points?

1) If a single API call sends a 6k-token prompt and the response is 2k tokens, how are tokens counted toward monthly usage? Is it prompt+completion or rounded per-call?

2) We have long-running chat sessions that maintain a context window by customer (context-siloing). Do cached prefixes / KV cache hits reduce billed input tokens or only reduce latency?

3) What is the minimum billing quantum? The draft mentions a 64-token minimum — is that per-call, per-minute of session, or per-token-window?

4) On rounding: do you round up to the nearest billing unit on each call, or aggregate per-session/day? We run millions of small calls and rounding assumptions materially change cost.

I attached a small usage snapshot and our proposed pricing table to illustrate our volume.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Harris
Head of Procurement
BrightCart Inc.

--
Attachment: usage_snapshot_Q1.csv (CSV, 28KB)
Attachment: proposed_pricing_table.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)

-----Reply from Jordan Blake-----
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@brightcart.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on billing granularity and minimums

Hi Tom — great questions. I pulled in Monica (pricing) and Karthik (dedicated contracts) to make sure we answer with concrete numbers. Below are short answers + we'll follow up with a short screen share if helpful.

1) Token accounting: We bill for total tokens associated with a request: prompt tokens + completion tokens. Each API call is metered at call-time; we do not bill the prompt separately later. Example: 6k prompt + 2k completion => billed as 8k tokens for that call.

2) Context-siloing / caching: KV cache and prefix caching reduce compute and therefore cost on Dedicated/private by lowering GPU cycles, but on the Hosted API the billing model remains per-token. That said, for customers on Dedicated plans we offer an optional "context discount" applied to repeated prefix tokens if you enable our prefix-deduping config. The discount is configurable by contract and requires a minimum commit.

3) Minimum quantum: The standard hosted minimum is 1 token (no artificial floor) — however, pricing tiers sometimes include a per-request floor for very small calls to avoid micropayment overhead. The 64-token floor you saw in the draft is a negotiated floor we proposed for low-commit pilots to keep rates predictable. For enterprise deals we can set a per-call minimum, or move to aggregated billing (per-session/day) to avoid per-call floors impacting cost.

4) Rounding policy: Hosted API default is per-call rounding to the nearest billing unit (for example, 256-token increments for certain legacy SKUs). We can change the increment / rounding policy at the contract level. Aggregated rounding (daily/session roll-up) is available for customers with committed volume; we provide a daily aggregation that sums raw tokens and rounds once per billing window, which often benefits high-frequency small calls.

I realize that's a lot — happy to show the arithmetic against your snapshot. Proposed next steps: 1) Monica to run the attached CSV through both the per-call and daily-aggregate models, 2) Jordan + Karthik schedule a 30-min call with you and procurement to decide which model aligns with your SLAs.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

-----Reply from Monica Patel-----
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Harris <tom.harris@brightcart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on billing granularity and minimums

Hi Tom — I ran your usage_snapshot_Q1.csv through three scenarios (attached shows summarized math):

A) Hosted, per-call rounding at 256-token increments (no discounts): monthly bill = $42,350
B) Hosted, daily aggregation rounding (one rounding per API-key per-day): monthly bill = $39,120
C) Dedicated with prefix-deduping enabled (contracted 500k tokens/day commit, context discount applied to repeated prefixes): estimated monthly bill = $28,700 (requires minimum 12-month commit)

Notes:
- The 256-token increment applies only to specific legacy SKUs; our newer metering can do 64-token increments or 1-token granularity depending on agreement.
- For the prefix-deduping math I assumed ~22% of prompt tokens were repeated prefixes across your model calls (based on the snapshot). If that's lower, the advantage shrinks.

Attachments: contract_redlines.pdf (I added a clause for per-billing-window rollup at the enterprise level), math_summary_v1.xlsx

If you want, we can provisionally switch your pilot to daily aggregation for the next billing cycle so you can validate the cost impact without changing the API.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Pricing & Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
